desc:
Back-end and API development builds the server side of your app: the database, the business rules and the endpoints your screens call. Ecom Swift LLC designs, builds, tests and deploys it on your own cloud account, with documentation your team can use.

## What is back-end and API development?

Back-end development is the work that happens on the server, behind every screen a user sees. It stores data, checks who is allowed to do what, runs the rules of your business and answers requests from a website or mobile app. An API is the set of defined doors, called endpoints, through which the front end asks the back end to do things.

When you press Save, load an order list or log in, the front end sends a request and the back end decides what is true. If that layer is weak, the app feels unreliable no matter how good it looks.

## Why does the back end matter for your app?

The back end holds your most valuable asset, your data, and enforces the rules that protect it. A careless design leads to duplicate records, slow screens, broken permissions and bugs that appear only when real users arrive. These problems are far harder to repair after launch than to avoid at the start.

A clean back end also makes everything else cheaper. A web front end, a mobile app and a partner integration can all call the same API. New features slot into a clear structure rather than being patched on.

## How it affects reliability, security and speed

Users judge an app by whether it works and whether it is fast. Good database design and sensible queries keep lists loading quickly as your data grows. Input checks stop bad or hostile data before it is stored. Tokens and permissions make sure each person sees only what belongs to them.

Logging and error alerts shorten the time between a problem happening and someone noticing it. That reduces lost work, support tickets and the quiet damage of an app that fails without telling anyone.

## What a great back end includes

- A data model drawn out before any code, with clear tables or collections and relationships.
- Endpoints with consistent naming, predictable responses and useful error messages.
- Login with tokens, secure password handling and, where needed, roles and permissions.
- Validation on every endpoint so malformed input is rejected early.
- Background jobs for slow tasks such as sending email or processing files.
- Automated tests on the main routes so changes do not break old behavior.
- Rate limits and security checks against abuse and common attacks.
- Logging and error alerts that point to the real cause of a failure.
- Written API notes, and a live documentation page for larger builds.
- Separate staging and production environments with a clean release process.

## What we do

We begin by listing the data you store and the actions your app must support. We design the data model, then build the endpoints, the login and the rules around them. Each part is tested before the next is added, and we write notes your front-end developer can follow.

The Basic package delivers a small API and database for one core feature. Standard adds more endpoints, roles and permissions, background jobs, email sending, automated tests and a staging deployment. Premium adds a larger set of endpoints, two outside integrations, rate limits, logging with error alerts, a live documentation page and a production release with handover. Add-ons include extra endpoints, an admin API and a documentation site.

## What to do and what to avoid

**Do:**
- List every kind of record your app needs to store.
- Decide early who can see and change each kind of record.
- Keep secrets such as keys in protected settings, not in code.
- Run the API on staging before you point real users at it.
- Keep the code and cloud account under your own ownership.

**Avoid:**
- Enforcing business rules only in the browser, where a determined user can skip them.
- Returning more data than a screen needs.
- Skipping tests on payment, login and permission routes.
- Sharing one all-powerful key across every service.
- Changing the data model late without a migration plan.

## Who it is for

This service suits a founder with a designed front end and nothing behind it, a business whose existing API has become slow or unsafe, and a development team that needs an extra pair of hands to build the server side of a project.

## What we need from you

Send the feature list or screens the API must support, any existing front-end code, and details of outside services to connect. We never ask for passwords. For deployment, you add us as a collaborator or developer user on your cloud and code accounts, and you control that access.
